faqs.a:
(a)
Administrative hearing.
A hearing held because of a petition filed under
section 14-204
(b) of this article will be conducted by the municipal court as an administrative
               hearing. Formal rules of evidence will not apply, but the court will allow the parties
               to call witnesses, present evidence, and utilize the right of cross-examination. Evidentiary
               and other questions will be resolved under the administrative hearing rules set forth
               in chapter 2 of this Code.
(b)
Owner fails to appear.
If the owner does not appear for the hearing, the court may proceed with the hearing,
               receive testimony and other evidence, make findings of fact and conclusions of law,
               and issue orders relating to the matter.
(c)
Hearing.
At the hearing, the court will determine as appropriate:
(1)
Probable cause.
Whether there existed sufficient probable cause for the impoundment, unless a warrant
               issued in accordance with this chapter authorized seizure of the impounded animal
               or animals, in which case, the warrant constitutes prima facie evidence of sufficient
               probable cause for impoundment; and
(2)
Costs of impoundment, care, and provision.
Whether costs associated with the impoundment of, care of, and provision for the
               animal, as determined by the animal management officer and the animal shelter are
               fair, reasonable, and necessary. All such costs must be itemized by the animal management
               officer or the animal shelter to the date of the hearing and must include, at a minimum,
               an accounting of the costs for the impoundment of, care of, and provision for, and
               any veterinary services rendered to the animal. An itemized account of these costs
               will constitute prima facie evidence that the costs shown therein are fair, reasonable,
               and necessary.
(d)
Considerations.
The court may consider the following in making determinations under
section 14-206
(c):
(1)
Impoundment circumstances.
The circumstances of the impoundment including the reason for the impoundment. This
               may include but is not limited to testimony and other evidence that the impounded
               animal was at large or otherwise not on the owner's or custodian's property;
(2)
Prior violations.
Any prior violations by the owner involving the animal or animals and the date of
               the violations;
(3)
Prior impoundment.
Any prior impoundment of the owner's animals;
(4)
Corrective measures.
The sufficiency of any confinement measures instituted by the owner and in place
               to secure the animal to avoid future at large or other violations;
(5)
Costs, charges, and fees.
Information about costs, charges, and fees related to the impoundment and care and
               provision for the animal; and
(6)
Other relevant evidence.
Any other evidence deemed relevant by the court.
(e)
Court's determination; contents of orders.
If the court finds there existed sufficient probable cause for impoundment, the animal
               will be held at the animal shelter until further order of the court. If the court
               finds that all or a portion of the costs of impoundment or care and provision for
               the animal are reasonable, the court will order the custodian or owner to pay those
               costs to the court within 72 hours of the hearing. If the amount is not paid to the
               court within that time, the animal will be considered abandoned as of the day after
               the payment was due. In this case, the court will on its own motion and by written
               order deem the animal to be the property of the animal shelter and order the shelter
               to destroy the animal, make it available for adoption, or otherwise dispose of the
               animal. Failure to pay these costs results in the forfeiture of the right to contest
               these costs and any ownership rights to the impounded animal.
(1)
Continuing costs of care.
If the owner or custodian wishes to prevent disposition of the animal by the shelter,
               the owner or custodian must file with the court an additional payment sufficient to
               pay for an additional 30 days of care and provision for the impounded animal. This
               additional payment must be filed with the court at least seven days prior to the expiration
               of the previous payment. This obligation continues until the owner or custodian is
               either acquitted or convicted in the municipal court of the charges relating to the
               impoundment and otherwise in accordance with the provisions set forth in this article.
(2)
Failure to pay continuing costs.
Should an owner or custodian fail to pay the continuing costs of care and provision
               for an impounded animal as described in subsection (e)(1) of this section, the animal
               will be considered abandoned as of the day after the last payment was due. In this
               case, the court will on its own motion and by written order deem the animal to be
               the property of the animal shelter and order the shelter to destroy the animal, make
               it available for adoption, or otherwise dispose of the animal. Failure to pay continuing
               costs results in the forfeiture of the right to contest those costs and any ownership
               rights to the impounded animal.
(
Ord. No. 4878
, § 9, 10-7-2024)
